why: Rule 1 read at cluster level: the deg-3 hub at the lowest z in the event has three prongs all stopping away from it (8.2 cm textbook proton Bragg 35k->300k to 84093, 11.6 cm rising 85k->175k to 84094, 4.2 cm flat 113k hot stub to 84099) with a MIP-level centre, while the rival 9004 is a 162 deg back-to-back pair (collinearity trap) whose long prong peaks in its middle, not at its far end.

Rule 1 at full strength: deg-3 vertex with 3 of 3 attached segments rising away (89 cm proton to 200752 at 19007, 50.6 cm to 117403, 25.9 cm to 57580), prong openings 64/69/11 deg so no collinearity trap, and the zoom shows a clean three-prong star; cluster 11's 11002 instead has a 45 cm pi+ rising toward it, i.e. a stopping point.

Rule 7 event (one big EM spray, 25 segments): 14001 is the upstream tip on the principal axis with 1 of 1 rising away and a 365k single-point stub at it followed by ~10 cm of 1-2 MIP before the shower onset, but the rival 14006 (deg 3, dense 130-205k core where the cone actually opens) sits only 15.6 cm away and both p6 verdicts on the connecting segment are driven by spikes, not Bragg shapes.

Rule 1: 2 of 2 attached segments rise away (88.7 cm rising to 237568 at the 19007 stop, 12.7 cm rising to 132327), prongs open at 64 deg so the collinearity trap does not apply, and the zoom shows a clean V apex with both arrows green at the lowest-z structured candidate.

Rule 1 plus rule 2: 19001 is a clean isolated cool free tip (53080, 1.2 MIP) at the upstream end of the event axis, and dQ/dx rises monotonically away from it along 45 cm (53k -> 97k/110k -> 235k) into the dense deg-5 junction 19013, which is 0 of 5 away and 3 rising toward it, i.e. the stop/interaction point rather than the origin.

Rule 1 with clean shapes: 2 of 2 prongs rise away at 116 deg opening from the lowest-z point of the cluster, and p4 shows seg 12042 flat near 95k for 30 cm then a monotone Bragg onto the proton template up to 250k at 12014, while seg 12043 leaves at 1.4 MIP and ends in a 380k blob at 12020.

Rule 3 excludes 18001 (the 51.2 cm muon leaves 18008 at exactly MIP, 42276, and Braggs to 200953 there, so that end is the stop), and 18008 is the deg-4 point where the single clean track ends and the branchy shower begins with 3 of 4 prongs at MIP; dropped one tier because the muon and the 25.6 cm prong leave it at 171 deg, the collinearity trap.

Rule 1: 15006 is the only candidate in the event with 3 of 3 segments rising away (cool 45k/17k/42k centre, far ends 69k/34k/131k) and its prong pairs are 144/141/53 deg, just under the collinearity threshold, whereas the rival junction 15002/15108 that carries the 40 cm and 18 cm MIP tracks is 0 of 3 away and hot at itself.

Rules 6/7 on a diffuse spray: the zoom shows a five-prong hadronic star at the upstream end of the event, three prongs terminating at free ends within 11 cm and several at 2.5-3.3 MIP, and the spray opens downstream from it; rule 1 reads only 1 of 5 away but the dQ/dx at a dense multi-prong junction is overlap-contaminated, and the only rival 22012 sits 20 cm downstream inside the spray.
